beats.text: Counting gives probabilities only after we identify equally likely outcomes. Two independent fair dice produce thirty-six ordered face pairs. The first die and second die have separate positions, so a two followed by a five differs from a five followed by a two.

Six ordered pairs add to seven: one and six, two and five, three and four, and their reversals. Divide those six favorable outcomes by the thirty-six equally likely pairs. We count the underlying outcomes before grouping them by their sum.

The possible sums themselves are not equally likely. Only one ordered pair produces two, while six produce seven. This histogram shows how many pairs belong to each sum, preventing the mistake of assigning every possible sum the same probability.

Without replacement, later counts change. From four marked objects and two plain objects, the probability of two marked draws is four sixths times three fifths. After the first marked object stays out, only three marked objects remain among five.

practice.prompt: List the equally likely outcomes of two independent fair coin tosses. Find the probability of exactly one head.
practice.answer: HH, HT, TH, TT each have probability 1/4. Exactly one head occurs in HT or TH, giving 2/4=1/2.

practice.prompt: Find the probability that two independent fair dice have sum 4. List the favorable ordered pairs.
practice.answer: The pairs are (1,3), (2,2), and (3,1). The probability is 3/36=1/12.

practice.prompt: A bag has five marked and three plain objects. Draw two without replacement. Find the probability both are marked and explain the changed denominator.
practice.answer: (5/8)(4/7)=20/56=5/14. The second denominator is 7 because one object has been removed.

takeaway: Count equally likely underlying outcomes, and update the sample space when earlier choices remove possibilities.
scope: Dice counting, unequal grouped outcomes, and two draws without replacement.
title: Counting outcomes
objective: Choose an equally likely sample space and use combinatorial counting carefully.
